plain: To be a sign of what is coming, or to predict it

webster.text: Among the Romans, an officer whose duty was to foretell future events by the singing, chattering, flight and feeding of birds.

more.text: To predict or foretell; as, to augur ill success.

example.quote: Contemplating the union of sentiment now manifested so generally, as auguring harmony and happiness to our future course, I offer to our country sincere congratulations.
example.cite: Thomas Jefferson, Second Inaugural Address, Mar. 4, 1805
